tldr: Iran and Oman floated a proposal for a temporary Hormuz shipping channel, cracking oil hard (USO -4.58% to $126.15, WTI ~$81) and unwinding weeks of geopolitical risk premium -- the sharpest single-day move on the tape.

Gold and silver held their debasement-trade grind to a second straight 3-month-high session (GLD $428.07, SLV $62.32 / spot near $69.26) on the same Treasury-buyback dollar-softness mechanism -- the miners sleeve (GDX/SILJ/SLVP all +1.9-2.4%) keeps working regardless of the oil reversal.

US Consumer Confidence missed sharply (89.4 vs 90.3 consensus, prior revised down to 90.8, softest since January, Expectations Index into recession-signal territory) -- a genuine cautionary data point landing hours before today's Core PCE and Prelim GDP prints.

Treasury actually named specific China/HK entities (Sweet Ocean Industrial network) in the Iran-sanctions rollout, and Beijing threatened retaliation -- a real escalation vs. Monday's 'warned but not targeted' framing, adding genuine tail risk for the HK tech sleeve.

Bitcoin broke above $80,000 for the first time in roughly three months on the same debasement/short-covering narrative lifting gold -- best read as a levered extension of the metals trade, not a diversifier.

Michael Burry (Scion) disclosed on his Substack that he exited his entire Alibaba stake (citing the ~$10.2B dilutive share sale) and rotated into a large new JD.com position, while continuing to add AI-bubble shorts (Oracle, Micron, Nebius) -- Substack-only, not 13F-reportable.

regime.label: Cautious, event-dense grind: Hormuz de-escalates, Nvidia/PCE and Jackson Hole all still ahead
regime.oneLiner: Risk appetite firmed on the Hormuz de-escalation and a cooling VIX, but Nvidia's print tonight, Core PCE/GDP later today, and Warsh's Jackson Hole debut Friday are three consecutive binary catalysts keeping this a grind rather than a conviction re-risking.

topNews.headline: Iran sanctions escalate: Treasury names specific China/HK entities (Sweet Ocean Industrial network), Beijing threatens retaliation
topNews.actionable: The concrete escalation the book was watching for -- named HK entities plus a Beijing retaliation threat raises genuine tail risk for the HK tech sleeve (0700.HK/0981.HK/1810.HK) and reinforces gold/silver's geopolitical hedge bid.

topNews.headline: Gold prints a second straight 3-month high (~$4,697-4,710/oz), silver holds near $69.26
topNews.actionable: The breakout extended into today's PCE/GDP and Nvidia prints -- no reason to de-risk the miners sleeve pre-Asia-open.

topNews.headline: US Consumer Confidence misses badly: 89.4 vs 90.3 expected, weakest since January, Expectations Index in recession-signal territory
topNews.actionable: Reinforces the case for staying long the metals hedge and patient on the cash pile rather than chasing risk into a data-heavy 48 hours.

topNews.headline: Oil extends its slide (WTI ~$81) as Iran and Oman float an interim framework to reopen Hormuz shipping
topNews.actionable: A real de-escalation signal, not just profit-taking -- don't extrapolate this into a broader risk-off reversal for the gold/silver sleeve, whose driver (dollar debasement) is separate from the oil premium.

topNews.actionable: Confirms the next technical level the book flagged -- still best read as a levered extension of the metals trade rather than a standalone diversification signal.
